title: Vocal nitpicker diary + mini-ops bundle — customer feedback synthesis
body:
Purpose:
Quick, operational digest of small but recurring customer gripes (the ‘nitpickers’) + a bundled set of low-effort, high-confidence ops/UX patches we can try in a 2-week spike. Intended audience: CS, Eng (serving runtime + infra), Product-hosted-api.

Topline (so you can forward to eng leads):
- Several customers (mid-market and platform teams) report recurring 95th-pct latency blips and cache miss patterns for multi-turn chat that look like small configuration or routing mismatches rather than model issues.
- Impact: perceived instability -> throttling customers, some opting for Dedicated capacity to avoid surprises. Estimated revenue risk: 2–4 accounts at ~$12–25k/year each if not mitigated.
- Suggested bundle: 5 small probes (<= 5 engineer-days each) that together should reduce p95 blips and make failure modes visible in Console.

Raw voices / illustrative quotes (copied from CS threads and support transcripts):
- "We see random 700–1100ms spikes on short-turn chat; everything else is fine. It breaks our synchronous UX." — fintech-PROD
- "KV-cache seems to reset sometimes mid-session; assistant forgets context after a follow-up question." — marketplace-startup
- "We can tolerate occasional latency but need consistent tail behavior; current variability forces us to overprovision." — enterprise-platform

Observed signal (what we looked at):
- Representative tickets: CS-8421, CS-8612, CS-8760 (attached links above).
- Console traces show: sudden increase in seq_len=1 token time > 600ms, often correlated with route fallback to a CPU-hosted variant or cold KV-cache rebuild.
- KV-cache miss rate correlated to session churn: customers with short-lived sessions + many distinct conversation IDs have 3–4x higher miss rate.
- Not all spikes are model-related; many are routing or autoscaler-induced (bursting between dedicated pods and shared fallback).

Small, high-confidence patches (bundle for 2-week spike) — prioritized by expected impact / low effort:
1) Route-stability guard (eng-runtime) — 2d dev + 1d QA
   - Block simple route switching for a conversation window: if a conversation has > 1 ongoing session in last 30s, pin to same model-variant for 60s.
   - Rationale: prevents fallbacks during bursty interactions.
   - Metric to watch: p95 per-conversation latency down; route-change count per-session.
   - Linked: JIRA CS-8465 (spike).

2) KV-cache diagnostics flags (infra + console) — 3d dev + 1d UX
   - Add sampling that records KV-cache hit/miss per-token and surfaces top n session IDs with high miss rate in Console (toggle OFF by default).
   - Quick win: helps CS triage whether it's cache churn or upstream model latency.
   - Metric: cache_miss_ratio for top-n sessions.

3) Small fallback TTL tweak (serving-runtime) — 1d dev
   - Increase short-term pinned-variant TTL from 5s to 12s for bursty traffic patterns. Low blast radius.

4) Canary of lightweight prefix-caching for short-turn flows (optimize team) — 5d dev + 2d infra
   - For known short-turn heuristics, keep a tiny prefix cache (first N tokens) to avoid repeated encoder passes.
   - Expected: reduces avg per-token CPU for short sequences.

5) Customer-facing 'latency posture' doc + runbook (CS + product) — 2d
   - Short checklist for customers: how to set conversation IDs, recommended session TTL, expected latency ranges, and how to enable cache diagnostics.

Risk assessment / why these are safe:
- Minimal model code changes; mostly routing/TTL/diagnostics.
- Patches are reversible and feature-flagged.
- None require lowering model quality or switching quantization.

Quick numbers / back-of-envelope savings (if successful):
- Target: reduce reported p95 blips by ~40% for affected customers.
- If 50% of at-risk churn is avoided, ~$60–100k ARR preserved in short term (accounts identified in CS-8421/8612).

Experimental observability: what we need in Console/telemetry (short list)
- Per-session route-change events (count + reason).
- KV-cache hit/miss ratio sampled per 1k requests (toggleable).
- Alert rule: any single customer with > 3 route-changes in 5 minutes -> auto-ticket or CS alert.

Notes from quick sync with eng (Miguel) on 2026-04-20:
- Miguel: route-pin change is feasible, but we should be careful with autoscaler semantics (could increase warm pods). He suggests conservative TTL and a pilot on low-traffic zones.
- Ravi (infra): adding sampling to KV-cache is straightforward; we should ensure sample telemetry respects PII and rate limits.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Does increasing TTL lead to more underutilization of burst capacity? (mitigate with canary/metrics)
- For customers on Dedicated, is route-fallback happening differently? We should confirm via Dedicated telemetry.
- Are any of the tickets actually downstream SDK misuse (e.g., conversation_id not being sent)? Parallel ask: add SDK telemetry note in the runbook.

Immediate next actions (owner + ETA):
- CS: triage and attach 3 more representative traces to CS-8421 (owner: Asha) — ETA 2026-04-18.
- Eng-runtime: implement Route-stability guard spike (owner: Miguel) — ETA 2026-04-28.
- Infra: KV-cache diagnostics sampling PR (owner: Ravi) — ETA 2026-04-26.
- Product + CS: short 'latency posture' runbook draft (owner: Sofia) — ETA 2026-04-20.

If we can deliver the 5 probes within 2 weeks and enable diagnostics, we should be able to:
- Prove whether variability is routing/cache vs model.
- Reduce perceived instability and slow the Dedicated-migration churn signal.

Unresolved: a couple of tickets show heavy seq_len variability that might come from tokenization differences client-side. Add a small SDK instrument: log tokenizer name and version for sessions in sample mode. (low effort, add to runbook).

Appendix — shorthand triage checklist for CS reps:
- Collect Console trace id + session id + customer timestamp.
- Check route-change count for session in last 5m.
- Check cache_miss_ratio (if enabled).
- Ask customer: are you reusing conversation_id across turns? which SDK version?
- If route-change > 2 and cache_miss_ratio > 0.25 -> escalate to eng-runtime.

Slack threads and refs:
- #cs-runtime-latency (pinned: traces 04/12–04/14)
- #eng-runtime (thread: route-pin-proposal 04/20)

Callouts for product prioritization meeting:
- This is not a new feature ask; it's stability/telemetry. Recommend classifying as "operational quality" with medium priority and a small-capacity spike budget.

Notes to self / rough hypotheses (work-in-progress):
- Hypothesis A: short-turn flows suffer when autoscaler preemptively moves traffic to fallback when a pod reports slightly higher latency for a short window.
- Hypothesis B: session churn combined with small prefix tokenizers causes cache churn (small memory footprint but high key-rotation).

End — will update after the spike PRs land and we have the KV-cache diagnostic surfaced in Console.

Quick contact list: Asha Kapoor (owner), Miguel Torres (eng-runtime), Ravi Narayanan (infra), Sofia Berg (product).

——
